ctx.x: When Bill Coleman went and Herman Chitterson and those guys.
Bill Coleman, Herman Chitterson, yes. Joe Hayman, yeah.
Well, Willie Lewis himself didn't go, as I recall.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I knew nothing about him but Cecil said that he was one of the best in the business and a fine arranger.

ctx.x: I was overwhelmed with joy at hearing and seeing this man who to my estimation played more trumpet than all the trumpet players I had heard put together, and the band was swinging like no band I had ever heard could do.

Cecil pointed out an alto sax player whom he told me was Benny Carter. I knew nothing about him but Cecil said that he was one of the best in the business and a fine arranger. But Benny didn't kill himself blowing that night. He wore a shade on his forehead to keep the bright light from shining in his eyes and sometimes held the sax to his mouth but not a finger was moving.

The banjo player was very good as were the rest of the rhythm section and it was surprising how the band swung along without the pianist. The drummer was another outstanding personality, especially during the floor show when there were fast numbers that the girls danced to and the finale which was very fast.
